question.:question/problem: Rewrite the expression $(z^{2} - 6z + 3^{2}) + 5$ as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{z}^{2}-2az+{a}^{2}=(z-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}-6z+{3}^{2} & = \\ {z}^{2}-2\cdot 3z+{3}^{2} & = \\ (z-3{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({z}^{2}-6z+{3}^{2})+5 & = \\ (z-3{)}^{2}+5 & .\end{aligned}
$$
